sections.text: O Prince! Purity prevails when Passion and Ignorance are overcome; Passion, when Purity and Ignorance are overcome; and Ignorance when it overcomes Purity and Passion.
When the light of knowledge gleams forth from all the gates of the body, then be sure that Purity prevails.
O best of Indians! Avarice, the impulse to act and the beginning of action itself are all due to the dominance of Passion.

So we had been discussing chapter 14, Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga. So we have seen so far that these three gunas are born out of Prakriti. They are actually the nature of Prakriti.
The nature gets it from Maya, as Vedanta says. Then Bhagavan Sankaratabodha says three Gunatmika Maya. This Maya has three gunas.
That which is not but appears to be -- that is Maya. So this Maya, which creates the illusion that this world is real, does so through these three qualities which bind our mind. How do we see a hologram? The question is, is the hologram real? A hologram has its own reality.
However, it is not what it appears to be. If I see a hologram of a woman, hologram is real, but the woman is not. So from that perspective, is this Prakriti real? Prakriti is very real, but it is not what it appears to be.
We have all learnt in physics by this time that the atom which appears to be solid and no real solid matter in it whatsoever, but it is very real from my perspective because it is a relative reality. So Bhagavan says in this chapter that all the beings which are born in this world are basically are born from the womb of Mother Nature, Prakriti. And I, this consciousness, I, the self, supreme self, Purusha is, is the seed giving father.
The entire Prakriti and entire creation that we know is born of the same entity, the self. The Purusha is the father and the Prakriti. The nature as we know is the mother.
This Prakriti has three gunas which bind the Purusha into the Prakriti. This union between the Prakriti and Purusha happens because of the three gunas in the Prakriti. And when that occurs, a being is born.
An ego is conditioned. Consciousness is conditioned, as we have seen in this analogy, a room space. When a building is built, it binds this space into it and the association creates a room Space.
The same way Bhagavan said Purusha came in contact with Prakriti, a conditioned ego is born. Three gunas we have seen is Sattva, Rajas and Tamas. Classic classification we heard over and over again. Sattva is the nature of purity, light, knowledge, illumination, Rajas activity, passion, attachment and Tamas, ignorance, inertia.
And then we have seen how each one binds this consciousness, which is pure and pristine in its nature. Once it comes in association with the Prakriti, it binds itself to the Prakriti and creates a new conditioned being. So verses 9, 10 and 11 give us this relationship.
Sattva binds you to happiness. This embodied one, this consciousness which feels embodied in myself, is bound by the nature of this field. We have seen this field -- Idam sariram Kshetram ITI abhidhya.
This body is the field. This field, with its three qualities, binds the consciousness in me. Sattva binds through happiness -- something happens, I figure it out, I come to know, I enjoy that experience. Rajas binds through activity -- the passion, the attachment creates desires, creates activity.
And the more I do, the more I achieve, the more I get bound. More and more I do, as Ill give an example. When I left India, I had one very clear goal: if I make a hundred thousand rupees, Ill go back to India and start practicing architecture there.
In Ahmedabad, I made a hundred thousand rupees long, long, long ago. Im still outside India. Rajas binds you to activity -- the more we do, the more I want to do. And then Tamas -- ignorance, inertia.
All three are absolutely necessary for this Prakriti to exist. Just as whatever ingredients bind the hologram into a form which I perceive must be there, so the next three verses summarize what we have already seen. Sattva sukhe Sanjayati Rajah Karmani Bharata Gnanam avrutya tu tamah pramade sanjayatu. Sattva binds to happiness and pleasure. Rajas binds to actions.
And this knowledge about the self -- the very fact that I call myself I, but Im not aware of what that is, I cant define it. As we have seen in this example: everything I use to define myself turns out to be something related to myself, but not me. My name, my relationship, my profession, my achievements, my losses -- whatever that is, its not me.
What is it that does not let me figure out who I am? Tamas. Gnanam Avritya tu Tamah Pramade Sanjayati -- by pramad, heedlessness. My own self tells me who I am, but this pramada, this heedlessness, says no, it cannot be.
Used to say, I come here every year. Because when He was alive, he used to come every year to the United States for Yagna. Some of us were standard devotees -- we were always there.
He said, Im glad that you guys are not listening to me. I come here, give you my knowledge, and on the last day I gather it and go back. That way you keep me in business -- because otherwise, once you understood, youd have no need for me.
This Tamas -- even though we hear, even though we understand, even though our conscience tells us this should be right, we say, But I dont think so, because not everybody else is doing it. So we get deluded by that -- Tamas, Pramade Sanjayati. So here is how he says that pure consciousness is bound into the Prakriti. Now, further analysis of how these three gunas work.
These three gunas are inherent in all of Prakriti. Tamas is not a negative quality of Prakriti -- it is the very essential nature of Prakriti. For an atom to remain in solid state, for me to recognize the atom, atom has to have certain inertia in it for me to see it as an atom.
If I can start seeing it as electron and proton and neutron, the world will disappear because there is no solid matter around. So the inertia, the Tamas is the essential quality of Prakriti. So is the rajas and so is the Sattva.
Because we have tendency to classify with the higher, lower and middle. So we say, well, this is higher, this is lower. For Prakriti there is nothing like higher or lower.
But what really matters is the right balance. How does one particular quality of this Maya bind me? Rajas Tamah Abhi Bhuyam Satvam Bhavati Bharata. One guna may be predominant at any given time, and the other two will be subsidiary.
How we recognize a thing or being depends on what the predominant quality is. For example, yesterday Sanchan -- normally hes a very nice guy, but I dont know what happened to him yesterday. In other words, normally he has this predominance of being nice, but once in a while the not-being-nice predominates.
Any guna can obviously have predominance over the others. When Sattva predominates over Rajas and Tamas, then the experience of Sattva happens. Right now, if I want to understand something, I focus on it, I close all my activity down.
Then the knowledge takes place, and we say Sattva is predominating -- everything is now clear to me. Raja satvam tamasteva tamah sattvam rajasthadha. Each one, when it predominates the others, makes that quality more apparent.
We may have any dish, and if there is more salt, well say its a salty dish. There may be a little sugar in it and all other things. But whatever is predominating, we call it that -- its salty, its sweet.
Even a sweet dish has lots of other ingredients and other tastes in it. At times Sattva predominates, at times Rajas, and at times Tamas -- in all beings, at least in human beings. Our mind, associating with the Prakriti, picks up whatever qualities attach most, and thats what defines our experience.
All of us go to downtown Richmond and we come back and describe it. All of us will have different description. Somebody like me will say, you know, the buildings are like this.
Each one will come back with a different impression. Because it is my mind associating with it, my mind experiencing this world of objects. Whatever the qualities I pick up is what my mind predominates.
There are times when Ill be dominated with Sattva. There are times rajas, there are times tamas. But the other two at that time are existing in a subsidiary role.
And the next verses tell us what happens -- and when I should recognize that I am under the influence of Sattva. Sarva dwareshu dehe asmin prakash upajayate -- if theres a light coming out of all the gates of my body. The navadvare puree dehi -- the body has nine gates.
Basically were talking about sense perception, the gnanendriya, the five senses of perception. Out of all these five gnanindriya, when there is a light of knowledge emitting, then I should know that gnanam yada tada vidya vibruddham satvam ITI uta. Im seeing clearly, Im hearing clearly, Im tasting the right things -- when Im having the experience of knowledge, the experience of light, then it is indeed the experience of Sattva.
It may be known that Sattva is predominant. There are times we are very clear about everything -- there is no confusion in our mind, no strong passion or desire to act, but simply to know. This is fairly logical, and we all have experienced that.
Somebody says, Rajan, I waved at you so many times when I was passing by, but you didnt acknowledge me. Oh, I didnt see you. My eye was not having any experience of knowledge -- in other words, the mind wasnt there, and there was no way to acknowledge what I was seeing.
All spouses know this. Meena will get mad and say, I dont like the insult. She says, Ive been telling you for the last two minutes and youre not paying attention.
No, no, I was paying attention, but I was doing something. It happens to me almost three or four times a week. Because my mind is somewhere else, shes continually telling me what happened, and then after about two minutes she realizes, I dont think he listens to anything that I say.
No knowledge is taking place. So thats not Sattva. Thats obviously my passion for something taking my mind away.
And it is so important for my mind to be there in everything. Once in a while I miss the verses which I chant, because within that fraction of a second my mind goes someplace else while Im chanting, and Im desperately seeking which verse I was on. Each verse ends with Guru Venama -- was I on the second verse? Was I on Guru Vai Namah, the third verse, or Guru Veh Namah? Because for a fraction of a second your mind lost it, lost the connection.
If that happens, its not Sattva which is chanting -- it is Rajas that predominated, because something took over. Lo Baha Pravruti Arambha -- now this is a very Indian concept, because its difficult for any Westerner to understand Pravritti Arambha. The urge to start something, to initiate action -- thats not Sattva.
Karmanam Asamaha Spriha Rajasya Jayante Vivruddhe Bharata -- these arise when Rajas is predominant. If this is happening, remember -- Bhagavan said, Im going to give you this knowledge which is so profound that, having known it, you will get rid of all your bondage and liberate yourself. Here is what hes telling us: how to diagnose yourself, what your situation is.
Otherwise, my mind constantly tells me, Rajan is a very nice guy. Hes a very Sattvic person. But he said, you have to do self-diagnosis, and you have to do it this way. The first sign is that there is knowledge coming out of all the gates.
It didnt say only one gate or the other -- all the gates.

These verses reveal a crucial insight: the gunas are constantly competing for dominance. Rajas tamash cha abhibhuya sattvam bhavati, Sattva prevails only by overcoming Rajas and Tamas, and likewise each guna rises by suppressing the others. This is not a static battle but a dynamic interplay happening moment to moment in your mind. Verse 11 gives a powerful diagnostic: sarvadvāreshu dehe asmin prakāśa upajāyate, when light (knowledge) streams through ALL the gates of your body (the senses), then Sattva is predominant. Notice the emphasis on ALL gates, partial clarity is not true Sattva. When you are truly sattvic, your seeing, hearing, tasting, touching, and smelling all convey clear knowledge.
The teaching illustrates this with everyday examples: waving to someone who doesnt acknowledge you, speaking to a spouse who doesnt hear, losing track of which verse youre chanting. These lapses reveal that your mind has been pulled elsewhere, Rajas or Tamas has taken over. Verse 12 lists the symptoms of Rajas: lobhah (greed), pravritti (the urge to act), ārambhah (initiating actions), aśamah (restlessness), and spriha (desire). Today, conduct an honest self-diagnosis: When do ALL your senses convey clear knowledge? When do you find yourself compulsively starting new projects or feeling unable to rest? Remember, this is not about judging yourself but about developing viveka (discrimination). The one who can accurately diagnose which guna is predominant is already beginning to stand apart from all three.
